Martin — thanks for the clear questions. Quick summary below, and I attached an index and a small telemetry sample for the adjudication example. Happy to jump on a call — we can do Mon 28th at 10:30 PT.

- Multi-region windowing: by default our SLA is region-bound (we report availability per logical region). For customers that require a weighted multi-region SLA we offer a region-weighted aggregation where availability is computed as the weighted mean of region availabilities using traffic-weighting supplied by the customer. We document weighting in the contract annex.

- Penalty model: we use a tiered credit curve based on monthly availability percentage (standard matrix: >=99.95% no credit; 99.9–99.95% 5% credit; 99.5–99.9% 10%; <99.5% escalation to remediation + potential 25% credit after adjudication). For burst windows (short spikes), we apply a rolling 1-minute probe alignment to avoid micro-flapping counting as downtime; sustained failures are measured on a 5-minute window for credit triggers.

- Measurement methodology: availability is derived from the union of synthetic probe pings and customer-requested telemetry where available. Our adjudication process correlates service-side telemetry (ingress egress logs, model host health) with synthetic probe outcomes. We provide both raw samples and a calculation workbook showing windowing, probe counts, and credit math.

- Evidence handoff: preferred mechanism is a time-limited S3 share for bulk evidence (we will provide signed checksums), combined with a summary workbook uploaded to the procurement portal. For highly regulated customers we can provide an encrypted archive + HMAC and a short signed attestation from our Reliability team.

Attached: slo-evidence-index.pdf (index of files), telemetry-sample.csv (anonymized snippet), redwood-sla-summary.xlsx (calculation example).

Next steps: confirm the call (Mon 28 10:30 PT) and we will prepare an expanded example matching Echoworks' traffic weighting.

Also we will need the evidence bundle to include a simple chain-of-custody note stating the artifacts were exported at a known UTC timestamp and checksummed. The S3 approach works, but procurement will only accept downloads with signed URLs and a digest.

Are you able to produce a one-page summary specifically mapping your matrix to our scoring rubric (we score heavily on per-route granularity)? If so please send before the call; it will speed approvals.
